title: SDK function compatibility stubs and streaming retry patterns
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Deliver a cross-language SDK layer that makes function/tool calling robust and ergonomic across Python, TypeScript, and Go. This ticket implements: (1) lightweight compatibility stubs that synthesize/normalize model-provided function schemas into language-native types and validators; (2) streaming invocation helpers that support chunked responses, resume tokens, and idempotent retry semantics; (3) telemetry hooks for per-invocation metrics (latency, tokens, validation failures) and structured error bubbling for apps to implement custom backoff/fallback. This work is intentionally split into a small language-agnostic core (schema normalizer + policy engine) and thin language-specific wrappers (type-coercion, idiomatic exceptions, example helpers).

Design notes and rationale:
- Schema normalization: model schemas vary in shape (open vs closed, required vs optional). Normalize to a canonical intermediate representation (fields with types, coercion hints, validators) so Python/TS/Go bindings share validation logic while retaining native casting.
- Idempotency and retries: streaming calls may produce partial side-effects in downstream tools. Default retry policy: up to 2 automatic retries for transient network errors if invocation marked idempotent; streaming-only resume supported when service sends a resume token (server-provided checkpoint). Non-idempotent invocations must bubble a RetryNotSafe error and expose an opt-in explicit retry helper.
- Streaming ergonomics: provide a single helper API that returns an async iterator/stream observable in each language, with built-in automatic chunk reassembly, transparent resume when resume token exists, and a small in-memory checkpoint to avoid reprocessing already-delivered bytes.
- Safety and observability: validation failures are surfaced as ValidationError that includes path, expected type, received value, and a suggestion (coercion applied or why it failed). All invocations emit telemetry events: invocation.start, invocation.validation_failure, invocation.retry, invocation.complete, invocation.fallback.

Example (Python):
from redwood_sdk import FunctionStub, StreamInvoker
# synthesized stub created by schema normalizer
math_stub = FunctionStub(name="safe_add", signature={"a": "int", "b": "int"}, idempotent=True)
async for chunk in StreamInvoker.invoke_stream(math_stub, args={"a": 1, "b": 2}):
    print(chunk)

Example (TypeScript):
const stub = makeStub({ name: 'upsert_customer', schema: ... , idempotent: false })
const stream = sdk.invokeAsAsyncIterable(stub, { body })
for await (const part of stream) { console.log(part) }

We will ship small example programs for each language in the examples/ folder and a migration doc for teams using older invoke helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Language-agnostic core that takes a model function schema and emits a canonical schema representation (unit tests covering coercion and edge cases)
Python/TS/Go wrappers that expose a function stub construct and a single-stream invocation helper with resume semantics and retry policy hooks
Telemetry events emitted for invocation lifecycle (start, validation_failure, retry, complete, fallback)
Integration tests using a fake model endpoint that simulates resume tokens, transient failures, and validation errors
Example apps for Python, TypeScript, and Go demonstrating idempotent vs non-idempotent retry handling
implementation_notes: Phase 1: implement canonical schema builder in Go (shared binary) + unit tests
Phase 2: add lightweight language bindings that call the canonical builder via a small FFI or generated JSON artifact
Phase 3: streaming helper implementation per-language; reuse existing streaming client where possible; add resume token processing and per-chunk de-duplication
Default retry policy implemented in policy engine with a configurable per-stub override (idempotent=true/false)
Expose 'force_retry' helper for non-idempotent calls that requires explicit developer confirmation and audit event emission
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema normalization edge cases: nested arrays, optional unions, and map[string,any] passthrough
Fuzz tests for input coercion based on historical model output shapes
Integration test harness that drives a fake model server to send resume tokens and cause intermittent network errors
End-to-end example smoke tests for Python/TS/Go examples in CI matrix
rollout_plan: Merge core library behind feature flag sdk.feature.fn_compat
Publish language wrappers as minor releases with clear migration notes
Opt-in rollout for internal customers (platform teams) for 2 weeks to validate telemetry and error modes
Flip default for new projects after 2-week opt-in window if no major issues reported
risks: Incorrect coercion may cause silent downstream errors — mitigated by strict validation mode and telemetry alerts
Resume semantics complexity: server-provided resume token formats may vary — require canonical token envelope and fallback to full-retry
Performance impact from validation on hot paths — will gate heavy validation behind a 'validate_args' flag and add sampling in telemetry
